title: Compact images and coproducts of the finite etale exceptional adjoint
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No separatedness of $X$ or $Y$ over $k$ is assumed. Fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{r}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $C$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$. On the ordinary unbounded etale derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], put $F=Rr_*j_!$.

Fix any right adjoint $G$ of $F$, with counit $\epsilon:FG\to1$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Assume that $F$ is exact and that there is an integer $N\ge0$ with $F(D^{[a,b]})\subset D^{[a,b+N]}$ for all integers $a\le b$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Assume also that the canonical projection map
$$L\otimes_C^L FK\longrightarrow F(f^*L\otimes_C^L K)$$
is invertible for every unbounded $L,K$, using derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact].

Call $E$ bounded constructible if only finitely many $H^i(E)$ are nonzero and each is a constructible sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]; say $E$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ if $E\otimes_C^L Q\in D^{[a,b]}$ for every module sheaf $Q$ in degree zero. For every bounded constructible $E$ of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, $FE$ is bounded constructible of Tor amplitude $[a,b+N]$ and is compact [def-pc-compact-object]. There is a set-indexed family $(E_s)$ of bounded constructible finite-Tor compact objects on $X$, all of whose $F$-images are compact, such that testing $\operatorname{Hom}(E_s[n],-)$ for all $s,n$ detects isomorphisms.

The right adjoint $G$ preserves arbitrary set-indexed coproducts and has the exact triangulated structure compatible with the fixed adjunction [def-weil-triangulated-category]: for every $n$ its shift comparison satisfies
$$\epsilon_{M[n]}=\epsilon_M[n]\circ c_{F,n,GM}\circ F(c_{G,n,M}).$$
For every $M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},C)$, the functors
$$V\longmapsto V_X\otimes_C^L GM,\qquad V\longmapsto G(V_Y\otimes_C^L M)$$
from $D(C\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], where $V_T$ is the termwise constant-sheaf complex [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], are exact and preserve arbitrary set-indexed coproducts, with their canonical composite shift structures. The constant-complex functor itself is exact and preserves these coproducts. Here $c_{H,n,Z}:H(Z[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}H(Z)[n]$ denotes the specified shift comparison of a functor $H$.

source.place: Section 6.4, Example 6.4.1 and Proposition 6.4.8, printed pp. 48–49, together with Definition 6.3.1: compactness input; retained item proof steps 5–7 give compact images, right-adjoint coproducts, and exact coefficient functors.

proof.text: Let $E$ be any bounded constructible input. For each of its finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves $H^q(E)$, apply the finite-type constructibility theorem to the separated morphism $f$ and the finite prime-to-$p$ coefficient ring $C$: $F(H^q(E))$ is bounded constructible. This theorem does not assume that $X$ or $Y$ is separated over $k$. Build $E$ from the finitely many $H^q(E)[-q]$ by the successive good-truncation triangles. Apply exact $F$ to these triangles. At each step of this finite induction, the cohomology long exact sequence expresses each new cohomology sheaf as an extension of a cokernel by a kernel of maps between constructible sheaves. The constructible Serre theorem gives constructibility, and the long exact sequence gives boundedness from the two already bounded terms. Starting at the zero truncation proves that $FE$ is bounded constructible. The Lean proof uses the existing boundedConstructible_obj_of_forall_singleFunctor theorem for this entire truncation induction and converts constructibility conventions using lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison. The finiteness theorem uses its own compactification; rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationIso transports the result to the specified c.

proof.text:
Suppose $E$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, and let $Q$ be any $C$-module sheaf on $Y$ in degree zero. Exact inverse image makes $f^*Q$ a module sheaf in degree zero, so $E\otimes_C^L f^*Q\in D^{[a,b]}$. Apply the assumed projection isomorphism with $L=Q$, and use symmetry of derived tensor on both sides, to obtain
$$FE\otimes_C^L Q\cong F(E\otimes_C^L f^*Q).$$
The assumed interval bound on $F$ puts the right side in $D^{[a,b+N]}$. This is exactly the asserted Tor amplitude for $FE$. No finite module is declared perfect, so the argument applies to nonregular $C$ as well. The definition also permits a>b: then E tensor f*Q is zero by disjoint t-structure bounds, so its F-image is zero and the assertion follows without applying the interval hypothesis to an unordered interval.

source.place: Definition 6.3.1 and Proposition 6.4.8: finite-Tor compactness input; the Tor interval is deduced here directly from the hypotheses by projection and symmetry.

proof.text: Apply the finite-ring compact-generator theorem on X and Y, obtaining the coproduct structures, local smallness, compactness criterion, and the bounded constructible finite-Tor detecting family E_s. Steps 1 and 2 show that every FE_s is compact. For an arbitrary input of Tor amplitude [a,b], even if a>b, enlarge its interval to [min(a,b),max(a,b)] before applying the compactness criterion to its F-image. For the shifted tests use compact_shift and compactObjects_isThick: compactness is stable under integer shifts and isomorphisms, and the given commShiftIso of F identifies F(E_s[n]) with F(E_s)[n]. No shifted constructibility or shifted Tor-amplitude lemma is required.

source.place: Example 6.4.1 and Proposition 6.4.8, printed pp. 48–49; finite-ring and nonseparated formulation in the cited compact-generator node.

proof.text:
Use the family indexed by $S\times\mathbf Z$, with objects $E_s[n]$, in the compact-test right-adjoint coproduct theorem for the fixed adjunction $F\dashv G$. All its assumptions were verified in the previous step, so $G$ preserves every set-indexed coproduct. Concretely, its canonical comparison $\bigoplus_iGM_i\to G(\bigoplus_iM_i)$, after applying $\operatorname{Hom}(E_s[n],-)$ and the adjunction, becomes the compactness comparison
$$\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(F(E_s[n]),M_i)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(F(E_s[n]),\bigoplus_iM_i).$$
It is bijective; detection therefore makes the original comparison an isomorphism. This includes the empty family.

source.place: Section 6.4 compactness; the adjunction Hom calculation is the cited abstract compact-test theorem. No general preservation of coproducts by right adjoints is assumed.

proof.text:
The adjunction-shift theorem supplies the unique coherent shift comparisons on $G$ compatible with those of the exact functor $F$ and with the fixed unit and counit. Its counit equation is precisely
$$\epsilon_{M[n]}=\epsilon_M[n]\circ c_{F,n,GM}\circ F(c_{G,n,M}).$$
The shift-compatible triangulated-right-adjoint theorem now gives exactness of $G$ with these very comparisons. Thus the exact structure used below is compatible with the originally fixed adjunction, not a separate choice of shift maps.

source.place: Tag 0A8D, lemma-adjoint-is-exact; existence, uniqueness and coherence of the compatible shifts are supplied by the first cited node.

proof.text: For T=X,Y the constant module-sheaf functor is additive and exact by constant presheaves and exact sheafification. Its mapDerivedCategory is triangulated by the exact-functor derived theorem. Apply the existing source theorem Adjunction.mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction to constantSheafΓAdj: the termwise constant derived functor has a right adjoint. This theorem derives the termwise homotopy adjunction using K-injective resolutions. Therefore the constant derived functor preserves colimits of every available shape in every indexing universe, directly by left-adjoint preservation. This replaces a termwise computation of derived sums.

source.place: Tag 03EI, lemma-sheafification-exact, and Section 03CS, section-presheaves-modules; termwise derived coproducts are injectives.tex, Tag 07D9, lemma-derived-products (1)–(2).

proof.text: For fixed M, tensoring with GM or M is triangulated by the existing tensor-triangulated instances. Closedness of the unbounded derived monoidal category, packaged by derivedTensorHomAdjunction, shows that left tensor is a left adjoint and preserves every available coproduct in every indexing universe. The canonical tensor symmetry transfers preservation to right tensor. Compose with the constant derived functors of step 6 and, on Y, with G from steps 4 and 5. The standard composition instances give triangulatedness, canonical composite shift structures, and coproduct preservation. This uses closedness directly rather than the one-universe specialization derivedTensor_preservesDirectSums.

source.place: Exactness of derived tensor and its direct-sum companion lem-kun-derived-tensor-direct-sums; composition with the functors established in steps 4–6.

proof_origin.place: Original seven-step compact-image and adjoint argument, implemented using existing truncation devissage, compact shift stability, the exact-left-derived adjunction for constants, and the derived tensor-Hom adjunction. Empty Tor intervals are handled by the zero object.
